owner: unassigned (to be named by the product owner)
interpretation: When a confirmed commitment limits the model providers that may receive customer content, any import, URL literal or gateway model identifier in scanned source that resolves to a registered provider outside the customer's allowlist is a finding.
approvedTextPatterns: Provider will route Customer Content for model inference only to the following model providers: <list>.
requiredFacts: The customer allowlist, as normalized provider IDs from the registry
A human-confirmed obligation citing the exact agreement text
prerequisites: Files are readable, under the size cap and not minified or generated
Only the listed TypeScript and JavaScript extensions are analyzed; files in the unsupported-language list yield unknown
falsePositiveExamples: A provider import in a test-only file that never ships
A provider referenced in code that is never executed
falseNegativeRisks: A provider that is not in the registry is not flagged
Dynamic specifiers such as require(name) or template literals with substitutions
Model identifiers held in variables or environment files
A proxy or wrapper module that hides the real provider
Configuration and environment files are not scanned in V1
URLs assembled by string concatenation, split new URL(...) arguments, or template literals whose provider host is not in the literal head
Hosts written without a scheme (api.openai.com) or as a subdomain of a registered host
Model identifiers passed anywhere other than the first string-literal argument of a declared constructor, for example generateText({ model: 'openai/gpt-5' })
Aliased constructors (const g = gateway), element access (gateway['languageModel']) and createGateway()('x')
Files whose extension is not TypeScript or JavaScript: the embedding formats reported unknown are covered, but .md, .json, .yaml and .env files are not scanned
Exclusion directories are matched by name at any depth, so a directory named like an exclusion is skipped wherever it sits
evidenceBoundaries: Findings show where source references a provider, not where traffic goes at runtime
nonClaims: Does not establish which provider receives data at runtime
Does not establish provider conduct, retention or training use
Does not detect dead code or proxy rerouting
Does not establish that the allowlist matches the signed agreement; a named human confirms that
Is not legal advice or a compliance certification
